name: pager-hang-avoidance
prompt: In this jj-managed repo, show me the operation log and current status so we can review before making changes.

assertions.description: Avoids the pager that hangs a non-interactive agent (jj pages output through less by default)
Uses the operation log to show what happened
Reports current working-copy status

name: describe-noninteractive
prompt: I finished editing the auth module in this jj repo. Record this as a change with the message 'fix: validate empty tokens'.

assertions.description: Uses -m directly, avoiding the bare describe/commit form that opens $EDITOR and hangs an agent
Uses the exact requested commit message

name: split-noninteractive
prompt: This jj change mixes a schema migration with unrelated test-fixture fixes. Split the test file changes into their own change with message 'test: fix fixture paths', non-interactively.

assertions.description: Uses jj split <path> -m, avoiding the interactive diff editor that plain 'jj split' launches
Uses the exact requested message for the split-out change

name: squash-noninteractive
prompt: Combine my last two jj changes into one, with the message 'feat: add rate limiter', without opening an editor.

assertions.description: Uses -m or --from/--into, avoiding the bare 'jj squash' / 'jj squash -i' forms that open an editor or TUI
Uses jj squash rather than an unrelated command

name: git-handoff-bookmark-push
prompt: My jj change is ready. Get it onto GitHub as a PR against main.

assertions.description: Creates a named bookmark first (jj's equivalent of a Git branch) before pushing
Pushes via 'jj git push', not a raw 'git push'
Opens the PR with gh once the bookmark is pushed

name: fetch-rebase-not-pull
prompt: How do I update my current jj change with the latest commits from origin/main? Git people would call this 'pulling'.

assertions.description: jj has no single 'pull' command; fetch is the first of the two-step equivalent
Rebases onto the fetched trunk as the second step, instead of a merge

name: colocated-no-raw-git-mutation
prompt: This repo has both a .git and a .jj directory. I need to stage and commit my fix. What commands do I run?

assertions.description: Mutates via jj commands in a colocated repo, instead of raw 'git add'/'git commit' which can desync the two
Names the colocated repo situation explicitly

name: recovery-undo-not-git-reset
prompt: My last `jj rebase` in this repo broke the working copy. How do I get back to how it was right before I ran that command, and what underlying mechanism makes that recovery possible?

assertions.description: Uses jj's reversible operation-log undo rather than a raw 'git reset --hard' (dangerous in a colocated repo)
References the operation log as the recovery mechanism

name: conflict-resolution-manual-markers
prompt: After a jj rebase, `jj status` shows a file marked '(conflict)'. Resolve it without launching any interactive merge tool.

assertions.description: Edits the conflict markers directly in the file rather than invoking a merge tool
Verifies resolution via 'jj resolve --list' or '-l', not bare 'jj resolve' which launches an interactive tool and hangs

name: parallel-agents-workspace-not-worktree
prompt: Two coding agents need to work on this jj repo at the same time without interfering with each other's working copy. What's the jj-native way to set this up?

assertions.description: Uses jj's native workspace mechanism for concurrent working copies, rather than a git-worktree-style answer
States the one-workspace-per-agent rule — never share a single working copy across concurrent agents

name: detect-colocated-state
prompt: Before touching this repository, how do I tell whether it's a plain git repo, a jj repo, or a colocated jj+git repo?

assertions.description: Checks for the .jj directory as the discriminator
Names the colocated (.jj AND .git present) case explicitly

name: snapshot-not-continuous
prompt: I edited three files in this jj repo but haven't run any jj command yet. Are my edits already safe in the operation log if the agent session crashes right now?

assertions.description: Corrects the myth that jj auto-saves continuously — it snapshots the working copy only when a jj command runs
Recommends running a jj command (e.g. status) to capture the edits

name: verify-before-done
prompt: You just finished a jj-based change and want to tell the user it's ready to merge. What must you check and report first?

assertions.description: Reports working-copy status, or runs the verification script, as part of the verification gate
Reports the change graph, or runs the verification script, as part of the verification gate
Also cross-checks with read-only git status (or the verification script), since Git is the canonical PR/CI interface

name: hook-recipe-session-safety
prompt: Set up this jj repo so that an agent's edits are always captured in the operation log at session start, even if the agent forgets to run a jj command first.

assertions.description: Wires a hook at session start (Claude Code settings.json) that runs a jj command to force a snapshot
The hook command itself is a jj status (or similar) invocation

name: identity-signing-ci
prompt: Running jj inside a fresh CI container to make a signed commit — what do I need to configure first, since jj won't pick up my git config automatically?

assertions.description: jj does not read git's user.name automatically; it must be set explicitly
jj does not read git's user.email automatically; it must be set explicitly
Addresses the signing configuration needed for signed commits
